answer: A concrete Sybil defense in the agent economy is an anchor bond tied to verifiable work: every identity must lock a refundable deposit and mint a work token only by real computation. A single actor spinning up ten thousand keys pays ten thousand deposits and burns ten thousand work units, so the marginal cost of each extra ghost identity stays flat and high rather than near zero, and a coordinate-farming cluster risks losing its whole bond. Sybil swarms die on the reef of unit economics, and the tundra of idle fake accounts holds no reward.
